name: Abandonment of the Fresno River reservation (reported November 19, 1859)
nations: Chukchansi Yokuts (Picayune Rancheria, Table Mountain Rancheria)
Poho-neche (as Royce names them), a people of the southern Sierra
promises: This entry records no promise. Royce lists it as the date Superintendent McDuffie reported the abandonment of the Fresno River reservation. Royce's note says the reserve was a farm rented from private parties since 1854, first set up as a temporary reserve, which Superintendent Henley reported in 1857 he had selected as the last of the five permanent reserves authorized by the Act of March 3, 1853. Royce's index lists these peoples under April 29, 1851 as well as November 19, 1859.
today: The Indian Claims Commission held in 1959 that the original Indian title to lands in "Area B" of California, which is all of the state except the areas of the tribes the order names, was extinguished by the United States under the Act of March 3, 1851. That holding concerns the land of the whole region, not the Fresno River reservation or any treaty promise.

nationVoice.summary: The Rancheria says the Chukchansi were among the tribes that signed the Treaty of Camp Barbour on April 29, 1851, that the lands promised in it were never given and the treaty never ratified, and that new reservations were then set up on the Fresno River where Hensley Lake is now.

sources.title: Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (1899), schedule text
Indians of California v. United States, Dockets 31 and 37, Interlocutory Order (July 31, 1959)

openQuestions: The treaty these peoples signed in 1851 is a separate entry (cession-1851-04-29-cas-son-cho-e-nem-nee-cho-ki-men-a-chook); nothing is taken from it here.
Decision for Jordan: an abandonment of a reservation reported by a superintendent is not a treaty; the card might better point to the 1851 treaty entry than carry its own status.
Whether the Fresno River reserve acreage was excluded from the Area B valuation, and the terms of the later California settlement, were not traced.
Secondary sources date the closure to 1859 or 1860; the North Fork Rancheria history page would not load for checking.

Audit 2026-11-08: promise rewritten from Royce's own note on the Fresno River reserve (Area 423): the earlier text said the reserve was set up for the parties to the 1851 treaty made at Camp Barbour, which the sources opened do not say. Removed the unsourced statement that none of the Area A tribes were in the Fresno River country.
